name: Dell XE9785L 8xMI355X, MLPerf Inference v6.1 Server: Llama 3.1 8B aggregate output throughput under the Server latency constraint
unit: output tokens/s (aggregate, harness 'Completed tokens per second')
methodology: AGGREGATE. MLPerf Inference v6.1 Closed division, Datacenter suite, SERVER scenario. LOADS: target_qps 0.5 Poisson arrivals, min_duration 120000 ms, compiled-in per-query TTFT/TPOT 99th-percentile bounds, 'Performance constraints satisfied : Yes', TTFT and TPOT early stopping both successful. Batch size not a fixed published number. Completed samples per second 1157.99. Model shape GEN_LEN 8127480. The full latency distribution is preserved in the source log and is unusually informative: min 1.758 s, mean 8.146 s, p50 8.308 s, p90 8.929 s, p95 9.095 s, p97 9.207 s, p99 9.428 s, max 10.647 s. POWER: has_power=False, design_power_watts=null, no declared cap. OMITTED BY SOURCE: TP size, KV dtype, concurrency, clock state, cooling.
notes: 6.2% below Offline (158458 -> 148563.48) - the largest single-node scenario discount in this round, and the reason is visible in the latency block: this run holds an 8.1 s mean with a tight 9.4 s p99, i.e. it is deliberately running long generations to keep the tail inside the Server bound. The p99/p50 ratio is only 1.13, which is the Server scenario working as designed. Worth recording for the tail numbers as much as the throughput: they are what a production SLO conversation actually needs, and they are here because the benchmark forces them to be published.
